2. How does PoR account for real-time backing during extreme volatility, and what cryptographic proof can users check that their token tier is 100% backed right now?

Binance maintains Proof of Reserves so users can verify that customer assets are backed, and users can check this through our official Proof of Reserves page and the self-verification tools provided there.

Our Proof of Reserves uses cryptographic methods, including Merkle Tree-based verification, to allow users to confirm their account balances were included in the snapshot. Reserve ratios and supported asset data are updated periodically on the official page, where users can review the latest available information.

Because Proof of Reserves is based on published snapshots rather than a live real-time feed, it should be understood as a transparency tool that helps users verify asset backing at the time of reporting. During periods of market volatility, Binance continues to manage reserves and user liabilities accordingly, while published PoR data reflects the most recent reporting cycle rather than an instant real-time state.

Independent assurance and review details, including methodology and reporting cadence where applicable, are also communicated through Binance’s official channels and Proof of Reserves materials. For the latest snapshot, supported assets, and verification steps, users should refer to Binance’s official Proof of Reserves resources.

1. Are my funds/user assets safe? Did users lose money?

User assets remain secure, and Binance has completed coverage of hacked assets in the security incident. Binance absorbed the impact so users did not bear the loss.

tweets.text:
Grok Bot summary of SpaceX CFO Bret Johnsen's interview with Gavin Baker.

🚀 Starship Flight 15
• Bret called it a critical milestone: the first time anyone has ever brought back a second stage.
• The ship deployed 26 satellites, then flipped and was caught by the tower's arms.
• Full reusability is the "holy grail of rocketry." He expects another 10x drop in cost per kg to orbit, with each flight costing little more than fuel and operations.
• Gavin's tip: take your kids to see a launch. Anyone can watch from the town beach near Starbase.

🛰️ Orbital Compute
• He called Flight 15 the big milestone for orbital compute.
• In the next year or two, compute in space should become cheaper than compute on Earth.
• The first orbital compute satellites fly next year, the constellation ramps in 2028, and meaningful gigawatts arrive in 2029.
• It runs on clean energy, raises no community concerns, and doesn't touch anyone's power or water.
• Operating costs in space are basically zero: no energy, cooling or land costs. The main cost is the launch.
• The satellites build on Starlink V3: swap the comms hardware for GPUs, then add more solar and a radiator that unfolds on the back.
• GPUs are burned in before flight, so reliability is very high.
• SpaceX has already flown 11,000 satellites, and laser links, shielding and radiative cooling are already proven on Starlink.

💰 Compute Economics
• SpaceX builds terrestrial compute for about $30–35 per watt, versus roughly $50–60 for the rest of the industry.
• Of about $50B per gigawatt, roughly half is chips. Once launch costs fall below the other ~$25B (land, power, building and cooling), space wins "big time."

⚡ Terrestrial Compute & Power
• Elon saw early on that power would be the main limit on AI compute.
• SpaceX spent the last year building its own power generation and is now a go-to for the industry.
• Turbine blades and vanes had an 18–24 month wait, so SpaceX is building its own investment casting facility to make them.
• If it hits next year's guidance, it could be one of the largest AI infrastructure players, if not the largest.

🏦 Financing & Cash Flow
• Hosting deals pay back in less than a year, sometimes much less.
• Most of the build-out can be funded by operating cash flow, customer deposits and longer payment terms from vendors.
• Funding so far includes investment-grade bonds in June and a $40B GPU financing facility with Apollo and Goldman Sachs.

📈 Demand
• Bret sees "nothing other than increased demand" for compute.
• Because SpaceX builds fast, it didn't need long-term contracts. That lets it sell compute closer to spot-market prices and earn higher returns.
• On Anthropic moving compute in-house, he said there are "no magic wands." Their growth plans will need far more compute, not less.

🤖 Grok Bot, Grok & Cursor
• Bret called Grok Bot "probably the best agentic AI solution out there."
• Gavin said he has made over 30 bots, and Grok Bot is on track to pass X in his screen time.
• Gavin estimated SpaceX isn't far from $10B in first-party software revenue. Bret just smiled.
• He said Cursor brings world-class product, sales and distribution talent.
• Grok 4.8 and 4.9 are coming "soon."

📱 Starlink & Direct-to-Cell
• More than 13 million people are now connected through Starlink.
• SpaceX now has two sets of spectrum: EchoStar's and the low-band spectrum it announced recently.
• It is working with regulators and carriers worldwide toward the first global wireless network.
• No big cell towers are needed: small cells can link back through space instead of fiber.

🌎 Impact & the Future
• SpaceX is spending a couple hundred million dollars on a desalination plant to bring clean water to Brownsville.
• Bret's proudest moment was turning on Starlink for a school in the Brazilian Amazon that had never had internet.
• He agrees with Elon's vision of a future of abundance, and said SpaceX is bringing building back to America.
